title: Pung-Plues Creek
summary: Pung-Plues is recorded as a small creek at Moriches in Brookhaven. In a 1681 deed, it formed the western boundary of a small neck of land and meadow near Watchogue and the bay.
history_content: The placename belongs to the Moriches neck-and-creek landscape. The dated deed reference is handled as a timeline entry with its source reference.
translation_content:
No separate linguistic translation is given for Pung-Plues. The name is treated as connected with Pung-plue, a Native person who likely lived at the neck.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names are the names that Indigenous people assign to various features on the land, and they are windows into the culture and history of people who have long lived there.”

— Alestine Andre, Ingrid Kritsch, Kristi Benson, and Sharon Snowshoe, An Indigenous Place Names Handbook: Sharing the Gwich'in Experience in Canada (2023), PDF page 6, Executive summary
preservation_content: Pung-Plues preserves a small creek boundary from a Moriches deed, showing how personal names, necks, meadows, islands, and creek lines structured local land descriptions.
